As in the world of products, the frequency of the consumer's need differentiates the quality of the competitive advantage.

points.title: Can the company repurchase shares to investors' advantage?
points.question: A good sign that a company has a DCA is that it will have a long history of buying back its shares. points.question: Does the company have right operational costs? The more durable a competitive advantage, the less a business has to spend to maintain it. Are large capital expenditures required to update plant and equipment? If they are building cars or designing software, they may not have to buy big expensive jets, or can use the same equipment for twenty years without any risk of obsolescence. If the answer is yes, be careful.

This will give you the investment's initial rate of return. Then compare the investment's initial rate of return and expected growth rate per share to the return being paid on U.S. treasury bonds. If the treasuries look juicier, the stock might be overpriced.

points.title: Projected annual compounding return as an equity/bond (Book Value model)
points.question: What is the company's projected annual compounding return as an equity/bond? Take the company's average per share return on equity for the last ten years and subtract the average percentage that is not retained and is paid out as a dividend. sections.heading: Porter's five forces
paragraphs: Competitive Rivalry: Moderate (3/5). Operating margin of 18.6% and ROCE of 7.0% set the intensity of competition. Healthy margins leave room for rational pricing behaviour among the leading players.
Supplier Power: Moderate (3/5). A gross margin of 36.6% implies suppliers capture the remaining 63.4% of revenue. A diversified supplier base and formulation ownership limit supplier leverage.

Buyer Power: Moderate (3/5). The gap between gross (36.6%) and operating (18.6%) margin shows how much value is spent winning and serving customers. A fragmented customer base limits any single buyer's negotiating leverage.
Threat Of Substitution: Low (2/5). Network Effects + Data Advantage is the primary defence. The product is embedded in customer workflows, which makes substitution costly.
Threat Of New Entry: Moderate (3/5). Scale, data, capital intensity of infrastructure and regulatory licences. keep new entrants at bay.
